meta.about: Nutrient limits and thresholds used by the scoring engine. Every number carries its source. Change thresholds here, not in code.

daily_limits.about: WHO adult guidance on a 2000 kcal reference diet. WHO says limits for children (2-15 years) should be adjusted down in line with their lower energy needs; this app scales them by child_energy_kcal / reference_energy_kcal as an approximation.

salt_g.label: Salt
salt_g.source: WHO: less than 5 g salt (2 g sodium) per day for adults

sugars_g.label: Sugar
sugars_g.source: WHO: free sugars below 10% of energy (about 50 g on 2000 kcal), ideally below 5% (about 25 g). Labels show total sugars, which can include natural milk/fruit sugar.

saturated_fat_g.label: Saturated fat
saturated_fat_g.source: WHO: saturated fat below 10% of energy (about 22 g on 2000 kcal)

trans_fat_g.label: Trans fat
trans_fat_g.source: WHO: trans fat below 1% of energy (about 2.2 g on 2000 kcal), ideally as close to zero as possible

fat_g.label: Total fat
fat_g.source: WHO: total fat below 30% of energy (about 67 g on 2000 kcal)

energy_kcal.label: Energy
energy_kcal.source: Reference intake for an average adult

fiber_g.label: Fibre
fiber_g.source: WHO (2023): at least 25 g of naturally occurring dietary fibre per day for adults

high_thresholds.about: A product is flagged HIGH in a nutrient above these per-100 g (solids) or per-100 ml (drinks) values. FSSAI has proposed red front-of-pack 'HIGH FAT / HIGH SUGAR / HIGH SALT' warnings but final thresholds were not notified at last review, so these interim values follow the UK Food Standards Agency front-of-pack 'high' criteria. Replace with FSSAI's numbers once notified.
high_thresholds.source: UK FSA front-of-pack nutrition labelling guidance (interim, pending final FSSAI thresholds)

low_thresholds.source: UK FSA front-of-pack nutrition labelling guidance

ingredient_flags.label: Hydrogenated fat (possible trans fat)
ingredient_flags.note: Hydrogenated fats can contain industrial trans fat, the most harmful kind of fat for the heart. FSSAI limits trans fat to 2% of fats and oils, but even small amounts eaten often add up.

ingredient_flags.label: Palm oil / palmolein
ingredient_flags.note: High in saturated fat. Common in fried snacks, biscuits and instant noodles.

ingredient_flags.label: Refined wheat flour (maida)
ingredient_flags.note: Most of the fibre is removed, so it is digested quickly and raises blood sugar faster than whole grains.

ingredient_flags.label: Added flavourings
ingredient_flags.note: Flavourings are a marker of ultra-processed food.

ingredient_flags.label: Caffeine
ingredient_flags.note: Not advised for children. Pregnant women are usually advised to keep caffeine under 200 mg a day.

ingredient_flags.label: Protein isolate / hydrolysed protein
ingredient_flags.note: Industrial ingredient; a marker of ultra-processing.

allergens.about: Keyword lists for common allergens. FSSAI (Labelling and Display) Regulations 2020 require declaring cereals containing gluten, crustaceans, milk, eggs, fish, peanuts, tree nuts, soybean and sulphites (10 mg/kg or more).

nova.about: Estimated NOVA processing group (1 = unprocessed, 4 = ultra-processed), following the published NOVA definitions. Estimated from the ingredient list, so treat it as indicative.

diets.about: Diet checks read the ingredient list and the FSSAI veg / non-veg mark. 'Vegetarian' follows the Indian meaning (no meat, fish or egg), which is what FSSAI's green mark certifies. Ingredient lists do not always reveal the source of an additive, so 'maybe' items are shown as a caution, not a verdict.
diets.jain_note: Jain practice varies between families (for example on dry ginger, turmeric or yeast); check anything flagged here against your own practice.
